n2-set-9-q-1.translation: Although their weight is within the standard range, many women worry that they are fat.

choices.reason: sui is not the reading of 標 in 標準.
sui is wrong for 標, and 準 is jun, not shun.
標準的 means standard or within the normal range.
hyou is right for 標, but 準 is voiced jun, not shun.

n2-set-9-q-2.translation: In the Diet, the struggle between the ruling and opposition parties continues.
n2-set-9-q-2.correctAnswerEnglish: 攻防 (koubou) - offense and defense; political struggle

choices.reason: 攻 is read kou in 攻防, not sei.
攻防 is read koubou and describes the back-and-forth contest between the two parties.
Both sei for 攻 and hou for 防 are wrong here.
攻 is kou, but 防 is bou, not hou, in this compound.

n2-set-9-q-3.translation: At a comprehensive medical checkup, a doctor can explain your test results in detail one-on-one.

choices.reason: とぼしい means scarce and is written 乏しい, not 詳しい.
ただしい means correct and is written 正しい, not 詳しい.
詳しい is read kuwashii; 詳しい説明 is a detailed explanation.
きびしい means strict and is written 厳しい, not 詳しい.

n2-set-9-q-4.translation: Many people argue that flaws in the entrance examination system cause the decline in university students' academic ability.

choices.reason: 欠陥 is read kekkan and means a structural defect in the system.
けってん is 欠点, a weak point; the printed second kanji is 陥.
けつぼう is 欠乏, shortage, not 欠陥.
けつらく is 欠落, omission or missing part, not 欠陥.

n2-set-9-q-5.translation: A standing roadside signboard has a considerable advertising effect.

choices.reason: 立て is tate, not date, in this compound.
立て看板 is read tatekanban: a signboard set upright beside the road.
看板 is kanban, not ganban, here.
Both date and ganban incorrectly voice the beginning of the two parts.

n2-set-9-q-6.translation: Although I decided which university to apply to, my confidence wavers as I wonder whether it is really the right choice.
n2-set-9-q-6.correctAnswerEnglish: 揺らぐ (yuragu) - waver or be shaken

choices.reason: 緩 means loosen, but 緩らぐ is not the spelling of emotional wavering.
揺らぐ describes uncertainty or wavering feelings after making a decision.
震 means tremble; 震らぐ is not the standard spelling of yuragu.
振 can mean shake or swing, but 振らぐ is not the spelling of this verb.

n2-set-9-q-7.translation: Life is a series of unexpected things, so you should not worry too much.
n2-set-9-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: 予期 (yoki) - expectation; 予期せぬ means unexpected

choices.reason: 与 means give; 与期 is not the word for expectation.
余 means remainder; 余期 is not the expected spelling.
世 means world or generation; 世期 is not 予期.
予期せぬ is a fixed expression meaning unforeseen or unexpected.

n2-set-9-q-8.translation: I was satisfied because this book was rich in content.
n2-set-9-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: 濃くて (kokute) - rich, dense or substantial

choices.reason: 内容が濃い means the book is rich or substantial in content.
巧 means skillful and does not spell 濃い, rich in content.
厚い means thick, but 厚くて is not the printed reading こくて and would refer to physical thickness.
密 means dense, but 密くて is not a standard form for the richness of the book.

n2-set-9-q-9.translation: Land mines are terrifying weapons that continue to target people indiscriminately for a long time.
n2-set-9-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: 狙い (nerai) - targeting or aiming at

choices.reason: 盗 means steal; 盗い is not the spelling of ねらい.
襲 means attack; 襲い is おそい, not ねらい.
狙う means to aim at; 狙い続ける means continue targeting.
追 means chase; 追い is おい, not ねらい.

n2-set-9-q-10.translation: On my way home, a man on a motorcycle snatched my bag.
n2-set-9-q-10.correctAnswerEnglish: 途中 (tochuu) - on the way; partway through

choices.reason: 避 means avoid; 避中 is not the word for being on the way home.
帰宅途中 means during the journey home.
道中 means during a journey, but is read douchuu, not とちゅう.
逐 means one by one; 逐中 is not the intended compound.

n2-set-9-q-11.translation: I did not learn my cooking from anyone; it is entirely my own style.
n2-set-9-q-11.correctAnswerEnglish: 自己流 (jikoryuu) - one's own way or self-taught style

choices.reason: 自己風 is not the fixed expression for a self-taught personal method.
自己法 is not the idiomatic compound for one's own cooking style.
自己流 means doing something in one's own way rather than learning it formally.
自己様 does not form the required word for a personal method.

n2-set-9-q-12.translation: People today are said to need enough exercise to walk ten thousand steps a day.

choices.reason: 運動料 would be a fee, not the amount of activity needed.
運動量 is the amount of physical activity; ten thousand steps indicate a quantity.
運動力 would be physical or athletic power, not the amount of daily exercise.
運動性 concerns mobility or properties, not a measured daily amount.

n2-set-9-q-13.translation: An interesting article appeared in the local section of the newspaper.
n2-set-9-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: 地方紙 (chihoushi) - local paper or local newspaper

choices.reason: 地方判 is not a term for a newspaper carrying local articles.
地方系 is not a newspaper term; 系 indicates a line or grouping.
地方番 is not the printed compound for a local paper.
地方紙 is a local newspaper, where an interesting article can appear.

n2-set-9-q-14.translation: Someone unexpected became the new company president.

choices.reason: 予想未 is not the compound meaning outside expectations.
予想下 is not the set expression for an unexpected appointment.
予想済 means already anticipated, contrary to the surprise.
予想外の人物 means an unexpected person or candidate.

n2-set-9-q-15.translation: As an only child, he has a strong tendency to depend on others.
n2-set-9-q-15.correctAnswerEnglish: 依頼心 (iraishin) - tendency to rely on others

choices.reason: 依頼心が強い describes a strong inclination to depend on others.
依頼性 is not the fixed expression for this character trait.
依頼力 would mean capacity to request, not a dependent disposition.
依頼内 is not a word for dependence or attitude.

n2-set-9-q-16.translation: My mother is absent-minded and often goes shopping without her wallet.
n2-set-9-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: そそっかしく (sosokkashiku) - carelessly or absent-mindedly

choices.reason: そそっかしい describes someone who makes careless slips such as forgetting a wallet.
にぶく means dull or slow and does not explain this careless omission.
おしく means regrettably or nearly, not forgetfully.
ずうずうしく means shamelessly; leaving the wallet behind is not impudence.

n2-set-9-q-17.translation: My sleep rhythm has gone out of sync, and lately I have been unable to sleep.
n2-set-9-q-17.correctAnswerEnglish: 狂って (kurutte) - become disordered or out of rhythm

choices.reason: 失って means having lost something; 睡眠のリズムが失って is not grammatical for a rhythm becoming disrupted.
リズムが狂う means a rhythm goes awry; it explains the insomnia.
送って means to send; 睡眠のリズムが送る is not meaningful here.
違って means to differ, but リズムが違う does not express a disrupted sleep cycle as precisely.

n2-set-9-q-18.translation: In this situation, it is a special case, so the insurance benefit will not be paid.

choices.reason: レース means race or lace, not an insurance circumstance.
ペース means pace, not the category of a claim.
リース means lease, unrelated to this insurance exception.
特殊なケース is a special case, explaining why the standard insurance payout does not apply.

n2-set-9-q-19.translation: Young people today are a generation that does not know the bubble era, when salaries kept rising steadily.
n2-set-9-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: 右肩上がり (migikata agari) - steadily rising

choices.reason: 盛り上がり means swelling or excitement; not the standard salary-trend phrase.
成り上がり describes someone rising in social status, not a salary trend.
右肩上がり describes an upward-sloping trend, here salaries increasing in the bubble era.
仕立上がり is not a term for a rising salary graph.

n2-set-9-q-20.translation: I did not look at your mobile phone on purpose; I mistook it for mine.
n2-set-9-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: わざと (wazato) - deliberately or on purpose

choices.reason: うっかり means inadvertently, but the denial contrasts deliberate spying with an innocent mix-up.
わざと見たのではなく explicitly denies intentionally looking at the other person's phone.
まさか expresses disbelief, not intentional action.
ふと means suddenly or by chance, not purposeful inspection.

n2-set-9-q-21.translation: Fatigue that doesn't easily go away often indicates an abnormality in the body.
n2-set-9-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: ijou / 異常 - abnormality or disorder.

choices.reason: 非常 means emergency or extreme, not a physical disorder.
体の異常 denotes an abnormal physical condition or illness.
救急 means emergency medical aid.
休息 means rest or repose.

n2-set-9-q-22.translation: Regardless of parents' economic means, the scholarship system should be expanded so that capable students can enter college.

choices.reason: 奨学金の制度 refers to the scholarship system for supporting students.
保証金 is a security deposit.
手付金 is earnest money or a deposit for a purchase.
入学金 is the one-time university admission fee.

n2-set-9-q-23.translation: As soon as he hung up the phone, he hurriedly left the room.
n2-set-9-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: awatadashiku / あわただしく - hurriedly or frantically.

choices.reason: さっさと means promptly or hurriedly, matching あわただしく.
うろうろと means wandering aimlessly.
そうっと means quietly or softly.
ゆうゆうと means calmly and leisurely.

n2-set-9-q-24.translation: Reversing the word order emphasizes the expression.
n2-set-9-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: sakasama / さかさま - upside down, reverse, inverted.

choices.reason: 変更 means modification or change.
考慮 means consideration.
逆に means conversely or in reverse, matching 語順をさかさまにして.
無視 means ignoring.

n2-set-9-q-25.translation: Preparations for the Olympics are progressing steadily.
n2-set-9-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: chakuchaku to / 着々と - steadily, step by step according to plan.

choices.reason: 順調に means smoothly or favorably, matching 着々と.
徐々に means gradually.
急速に means rapidly.
意外に means unexpectedly.

n2-set-9-q-26.translation: You should not take it lightly, saying it is merely a cold.
n2-set-9-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: amaku mite / 甘く見て - underestimating or letting one's guard down.

choices.reason: 中断して means interrupting.
停止して means halting.
変更して means altering.
油断して means being careless or letting one's guard down, matching 甘く見て.

n2-set-9-q-27.translation: Recent TV dramas have become stereotypical and lost their freshness.
n2-set-9-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: mannerika shite iru / マンネリ化している - stuck in a rut / lacking novelty.

choices.reason: 評判が悪い means having a bad reputation.
新鮮味がない means lacking freshness or originality, matching マンネリ化している.
人気がある means popular.
いい加減だ means irresponsible or half-hearted.

n2-set-9-q-28.translation: Estimating from the voice on the telephone, the perpetrator is a young man.
n2-set-9-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: suitei / 推定 - estimation, inference, presumption.

choices.reason: Estimating grief is unnatural; 想像できない fits.
Measuring blood pressure uses 測定 (sokutei), not 推定.
電話の声から推定すると correctly infers the culprit's profile based on evidence.
Investigating or guessing someone's secret uses 探る, not 推定.

n2-set-9-q-29.translation: Ever since graduating from university, I have completely neglected to contact my teacher.
n2-set-9-q-29.correctAnswerEnglish: gobusata / ごぶさた - neglect of contact, long absence.

choices.reason: Leaving late uses そろそろ失礼します, not ごぶさた.
Missing a meeting due to illness uses 欠席, not ごぶさた.
Apologizing for a sudden visit uses 突然お邪魔して, not ごぶさた.
先生にはすっかりごぶさたしている is the correct polite idiom for not having contacted someone for a long time.

n2-set-9-q-30.translation: Because he has a straightforward personality, I think he won't worry about minor details.
n2-set-9-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: tanjun / 単純 - simple, uncomplicated, ingenuous.

choices.reason: A simple meal uses 質素な or 簡単な, not 単純な.

Losing easily in round one uses あっさり or 簡単に, not 単純に.

n2-set-9-q-31.translation: Having drunk too much alcohol, my footing was unsteady and I couldn't walk alone.
n2-set-9-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: ashimoto / 足元 - at one's feet; 足元がふらつく means unsteady footing.

choices.reason: Living close to each other uses 近所 or 近く, not 足元.
足元がふらつく is the standard idiom for one's footing wobbling when drunk.
Leaving parents' care uses 親元を離れる, not 足元.
Nearby shops uses 近所の店, not 足元.

n2-set-9-q-32.translation: We built a house, but we considerably exceeded our initial budget, which is tough.
n2-set-9-q-32.correctAnswerEnglish: chouka / 超過 - exceeding, surpassing a limit/budget.

choices.reason: An increase in depression patients uses 増加, not 超過.
Taxis charging extra late-night fare uses 割増, not 超過.
予算をかなり超過してしまい correctly describes exceeding a numerical financial budget.
Taking too much medicine uses 過剰摂取 or 飲みすぎ, not 超過.

n2-set-9-q-33.translation: From long ago, towns have developed along the course of this river.
n2-set-9-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: ni sotte / に沿って - along / following the line of.

choices.reason: に連れて means as something progresses (correlative change), not parallel to a river.

に並べて is ungrammatical here.
に並んで means lined up with, not following the river course.

n2-set-9-q-34.translation: Residents' opinions were divided in two over whether to build a dam in the village.
n2-set-9-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: o megutte / をめぐって - concerning / surrounding a dispute.

choices.reason: を通じて means through or via.
をもとにして means based upon.
をまわって means going around physically.
〜をめぐって expresses conflict or debate surrounding a disputed topic.

n2-set-9-q-35.translation: When it came to teaching struggling children, there was no teacher more skilled than him.
n2-set-9-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: ni kakete wa / にかけては - when it comes to (someone's special skill).

にかかっては means if subjected to someone's influence.
にかかわっては means relating to / affecting.
につけては means whenever something happens.

n2-set-9-q-36.translation: If I could go on an overseas trip, I would definitely like to see the Egyptian pyramids.

としても means even if (concessive).
とすると introduces a logical calculation or consequence.
もし〜としたら naturally frames an imaginative hypothetical condition.

n2-set-9-q-37.translation: Without anyone dropping out until the very end, everyone was able to graduate.
n2-set-9-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: koto naku / ことなく - without doing.

choices.reason: 脱落することなく means without dropping out (formal equivalent of 脱落しないで).
わけなく means effortlessly.
しかなく means having no choice but to.
ほかなく also means having no alternative.

n2-set-9-q-38.translation: The result is already decided. Complaining about it now won't help.
n2-set-9-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: ittemo / 言っても - as in 〜てもはじまらない (it is no use doing).

言うなら means if you say.
言わなくても reverses the meaning.

n2-set-9-q-39.translation: Even if you have money, without health you cannot enjoy life.
n2-set-9-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: nakushite / なくして - without / in the absence of.

choices.reason: ならでは means unique to.
なかぎり is ungrammatical; ないかぎり would be needed.
〜なくして…ない expresses that something indispensable (health) is essential for an outcome.
ないでは is not the correct compound preposition.

n2-set-9-q-40.translation: Thank you very much for always viewing our company's website.
n2-set-9-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: goran itadaki / ごらんいただき - viewing (polite honorific for receiving the action of looking).

choices.reason: ごらんになられていただき is a double honorific error.

ごらんいただき is the standard respectful expression for a customer viewing a site.
見られてくださり is ungrammatical honorific phrasing.

n2-set-9-q-41.translation: This tree fruit isn't completely inedible, but it is not very tasty.
n2-set-9-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: koto mo nai / 食べられなくもないが - it is not that you can't eat it (it is edible).

choices.reason: 食べられたくもないが means does not want to be eaten.

食べたくもないが means doesn't even want to eat it.
食べたこともないが means has never eaten it.

n2-set-9-q-42.translation: Now that my subordinate is taking time off due to illness, I have no choice but to do his work instead.
n2-set-9-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: suru hoka nai / するほかない - have no other choice but to do.

しないわけない means impossible not to do, but misses the forced necessity idiom.

n2-set-9-q-43.translation: A: Are you doing anything for your health? B: Well, I make it a habit to go for a walk every day.
n2-set-9-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: iku koto ni shite imasu / 行くことにしています - make a personal habit of going.

choices.reason: 行くようになっています describes an external automatic process or change of state.
行ったようになっています implies pretending or an appearance.
散歩に行くことにしています expresses a conscious, self-determined daily habit.
行ったことにしています means pretending to have gone.

n2-set-9-q-44.translation: Even though it may be unavoidable that homes are expensive in Tokyo due to limited land, it is strange that you cannot buy one even working honestly all your life.
n2-set-9-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: shikata ga nai to wa ie / 高くてもしかたがないとはいえ - although it may be inevitable that it is expensive.

choices.reason: 高くてもかまわないが means it doesn't matter if it's expensive, contradicting the complaint.

高くてはかまわないが is ungrammatical.
高くてはしかたがない lacks the concessive 'とはいえ' needed before the criticism.

n2-set-9-q-45.translation: People say that having many children makes life tough, but precisely because I have children, I find the strength to work hard.
n2-set-9-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: to iu keredo / というけれど - option 4 sits at the star.

choices.reason: 子どもがいる follows というけれど and precedes からこそ in third position.
生活が苦しくなる follows 子どもがたくさんいると and comes first.
からこそ attaches to 子どもがいる and comes fourth.
というけれど comes second at the star position: 生活が苦しくなるというけれど子どもがいるからこそ.

n2-set-9-q-46.translation: As society becomes more affluent, the spirit of mutual help has grown weaker.
n2-set-9-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: naru ni tsure / なるにつれ - option 2 sits at the star.

choices.reason: 助け合いの気持ちが follows なるにつれ and comes third.
なるにつれ follows 豊かに and comes second at the star: 世の中が豊かになるにつれ助け合いの気持ちが.
豊かに begins after 世の中が and comes first.
薄く attaches to なってきた and comes fourth.

n2-set-9-q-47.translation: This house was also beautiful when it was built, but with the passage of time, repairs have become necessary in various places.
n2-set-9-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: toki / とき - option 3 sits at the star in ときとともに.

choices.reason: とともに follows とき and comes fourth.
ときは attaches to 建てた and comes first.
とき forms ときとともに ('with time') and comes third at the star position.
きれいだったが follows ときは and comes second.

n2-set-9-q-48.translation: A: What's for dinner today? B: Curry. Although I say curry, it's not ordinary curry but Indian style.
n2-set-9-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: ittemo / いっても - option 2 sits at the star in といっても.

choices.reason: 普通のカレー follows いっても and comes third.
いっても completes カレーといっても and comes second at the star position.
じゃなくて follows 普通のカレー and comes fourth.
と follows カレー and comes first.

n2-set-9-q-49.translation: If you don't have enough money, you probably have no other choice but to borrow from your parents.
n2-set-9-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: hoka / ほか - option 1 sits at the star in よりほかない.

choices.reason: ほか forms よりほかない ('no choice but to') and comes third at the star position.
より follows 借りる and comes second.
ない follows ほか and comes fourth.
借りる attaches to 親に and comes first.

n2-set-9-q-50.translation: While conversations overheard on trains and buses don't bother people at all, mobile phones feel unpleasant.
n2-set-9-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: ki ni naranai / 気にならない - not bothersome / does not concern.

choices.reason: 気にならない contrasts directly with 不快に感じてしまう ('even though normal talk doesn't bother us...').
気がつかない means does not notice.
気にする means to mind/care, which would make the contrasting 'のに' illogical.
気にいらない means dislike.

n2-set-9-q-51.translation: In face-to-face conversations, even if only roughly, we can understand the flow of talk, and if it is unnecessary information, we can ignore it.
n2-set-9-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: a rikai deki / b mushi suru - a understand / b ignore.

choices.reason: a 無視でき would mean we can ignore the flow, making b redundant.
a 理解でき / b 無視する perfectly fits the psychological mechanism: understanding context allows ignoring unnecessary input.
b 理解する contradicts the filter mechanism.
a 無視でき confuses the sequence.

n2-set-9-q-52.translation: However, toward things where we don't know what will happen next, we constantly pay attention.
n2-set-9-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: wakaranai mono / わからないもの - things that are unknown / unpredictable.

choices.reason: 想像できるもの means things we can imagine, which the text explicitly says we can ignore.
理解できるもの also contradicts the preceding contrast with predictable things.
無視できるもの contradicts the need to pay attention.
何が起こるかわからないもの matches the unpredictability that forces the brain to stay attentive.

n2-set-9-q-53.translation: Because only half of the conversation can be heard on a mobile phone, the brain subconsciously maintains a tense state trying to grasp the whole picture.
n2-set-9-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: hanbun dake / 半分だけ - only half.

choices.reason: 全部 means the whole thing, which is impossible since the other side is on the phone.
全然 means not at all.
話が半分だけ聞こえる describes hearing only one party's voice, driving the listener's brain tension.
半分しか requires a negative verb, but the verb is positive 聞こえる.

n2-set-9-q-54.translation: Using mobile phones on public transportation should probably be refrained from.
n2-set-9-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: hikaeru beki darou / 控えるべきだろう - ought to refrain from.

choices.reason: 控えてはならない means must not refrain, which is the exact opposite of avoiding irritation.
控えるものではない means it is not something one should avoid, also opposite.
控えるべきだろう concludes that one should exercise restraint in using phones on public transit.
控えるわけだろう is an unnatural conjecture pattern here.
